text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Tension in Likud party over report Prime Minister Netanyahu promised in the United States not to build Har Homa Jewish neighbourhood in East Jerusalem.
- Foreign Minister Levy says Israel will not hinder work of joint Israel-PLO negotiating committee.
- Government Corporations Authority will propose selling Bezeq Israel Telecom shares on Tel Aviv stock market instead of overseas.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu to testify tomorrow in attorney-general scandal investigation.
- Initial signs of revival in tourism to Israel.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu tells inner circle: This is not the time to build Har Homa.
- Bank of Israel's supervisor of banks says Bank Hapoalim can be sold within months.
- Israeli tobacco company Dubek will begin manufacturing cigarettes abroad for sale to Palestinian self-rule areas.
GLOBES
- Senior Israel Discount Bank officials say timing of publication of prospectus dictated by M.I. Holdings.
- Israel Aircraft Industries to supply 2,400 fireproof helicopter seats to U.S. navy.
- Drop of 17.6 percent in tourism to Israel in January compared with January 1996.
JERUSALEM POST
- Foreign Minister Levy upbeat as talks with PLO resume.
- Netanyahu discusses conversion bill with U.S. rabbis.
- No new building permits for Hebron settlers.
